title: A Healthy Twin Helps Sick Coral Get Better
summary:
Scientists found that badly bleached corals can get healthy again by touching healthy corals that are genetically identical, like twins. In lab tests, the sick corals recovered in seven weeks. The study came out on October 14 in the journal Science Advances.

Corals are animals. Tiny algae live inside them and give them food energy. When ocean water gets too warm, corals lose these algae and turn white. This is called bleaching.

The idea started by accident in 2025. In Stanford professor Steve Palumbi's lab, a healthy piece of coral fell against a bleached piece from the same coral. Where they touched, the bleached piece got its color back.

Student Danny Collins tested 10 pairs of coral pieces. Bleached pieces that touched their healthy partner all recovered. The ones kept apart died. The corals' tissues joined, and helpful algae moved across.

The researchers say this could lead to new ways to help coral reefs.
why_it_matters: Healthy coral reefs are homes for many sea animals that kids love to learn about.
